scenes.title: Villefranche-sur-Mer [vue générale]
scenes.description: A general view of Villefranche-sur-Mer, taken in 1912 by the Agence Rol press photography agency. The record identifies it as a press photograph, a negative on glass measuring 13 x 18 cm, held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France (National Library of France).
scenes.explanation: Personal watercraft like the jet ski were not invented until the 1970s, so one cannot appear in a 1912 harbor scene.

source.description: Référence bibliographique : Rol, 18910 Appartient à l’ensemble documentaire : Pho20Rol

scenes.title: 113 Trondhjem. Kongens gate
scenes.description: A photograph titled 113 Trondhjem. Kongens gate, held by the National Library of Norway and in the public domain, shows Kongens gate in Trondhjem in 1920. The record does not name the photographer.
scenes.explanation: Kick scooters as a common personal transport did not exist in 1920.
scenes.credit: Mittet & Co. AS via National Library of Norway

scenes.title: Penchot : voie, Lot, gare, tunnel, 4 juin
scenes.description: A photograph taken by Eugène Trutat on 4 June 1898 shows Penchot with its railway track, the Lot river, a station and a tunnel. The record identifies the location with Decazeville in Aveyron, France, and also lists subjects including a watercourse, a factory, hydraulic power, a riverbank, a railway, a station and a chimney.
scenes.explanation: Intermodal steel shipping containers were not used in rail freight until the 1950s, so one cannot appear in an 1898 photograph.

source.originalTitle: Penchot : voie, Lot, gare, tunnel, 4 juin 1898

scenes.title: Båtstø, Høvik brygge
scenes.description: A photograph titled Båtstø, Høvik brygge, held by the National Library of Norway and in the public domain, dating from 1920. The record does not name a photographer.
scenes.explanation: Utility-scale wind turbines did not exist in 1920; the first modern multi-megawatt turbines were built in the 1980s.
scenes.credit: Riksantikvaren via National Library of Norway

scenes.title: Manoeuvres, officier étrangers [un groupe devant un train]
scenes.description: A press photograph by Agence Rol showing a group of foreign officers in front of a train during the 1912 manoeuvres. Taken in France in September 1912, it is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France (reference Rol, 23441).
scenes.explanation: Compact folding strollers with small wheels did not exist in 1912, so this object could not be present on the platform.
